section_summary.extract_value: This General Discussion section emphasizes the importance of time in understanding the dynamic and nonlinear relationship between salesperson goal orientations (Learning Orientation and Performance Orientation) and performance adaptation during organizational change. The study found that Performance Orientation countervailed the effects of Learning Orientation on performance trajectories, with high-PO salespeople showing less initial decline but slower recovery. It also notes that a longitudinal design is crucial for capturing these complex dynamics, as cross-sectional analyses would yield incomplete conclusions. The section refers to 'This study' throughout, indicating a single study.

section_summary.extract_value: This section, titled 'General Discussion', emphasizes the importance of time in theories of performance and organizational change. It presents findings from 'This study' which examined the dynamic relationship between salesperson goal orientations (Learning Orientation and Performance Orientation) and performance adaptation over time, particularly during phases of organizational change (unfreezing, moving, refreezing). The study found that LO amplified performance changes, while PO countervailed these effects. Figure 3 illustrates the longitudinal influence of PO on salesperson performance trajectories.
